FIGURE 44-7  Child with cerebral palsy.
BOX 44-2  Different Types of Cerebral Palsy
Spastic CP: Increased muscle tone, persistent infant reflexes, in-
creased deep tendon reflexes in one of three patterns: hemiplegia 
(arm and leg on one side of the body), diplegia (involving the lower 
extremities), and quadriplegia (all four extremities and may include 
the trunk, head, and neck)
Dyskinetic CP: Abnormalities in muscle tone that affect the entire body; 
includes athetoid CP, which includes uncontrolled and continuous in-
voluntary movements
Mixed CP: A condition in which both athetosis and spasticity are present
Ataxic CP: Abnormalities of voluntary movement and balance such as 
unsteady gait
Athetoid dyskinetic CP: Normal intelligence but difficulty walking, 
sitting, speaking clearly
